turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Sir, please have a seat, doctor is just finishing a call. I will take the pressure and the pulse before he comes.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly, madam. I am sorry if we have come without a proper emergency. My wife was rather insistent.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): That is quite alright. Blood pressure is 152 over 88, pulse is 72, oxygen saturation 98 percent. I will leave the sheet on the desk.

[SEG0004] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, ah, you are here. I am his wife. He will say he is fine, but last Tuesday he got lost near the vegetable market, he repeats questions, and he is forgetting appointments.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): With due respect, that is not correct. The main road was crowded, so I took the longer lane. I was not lost.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): I caught the end of that. Let me think how to hold both versions. Madam, you live with him, and you see the day to day?
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes, we live together. He is a retired headmaster, seventy-four. I am the one who gives every tablet, morning and night.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not repeat myself, doctor. I am quite well, thank you. She has always been careful, perhaps a little more than required.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Um, so, repeating questions on one side, and a gentleman who feels well on the other. I am not choosing a label. What about the appointments, any missed?
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He forgot the dentist last month, and the eye check before that. Both were written on the calendar, I showed him.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I remember the dentist very well, we did go. The eye one, well, actually the clinic itself had shifted, so that was hardly my forgetting.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hmm, two stories again. Any headache with this, or is sleep broken?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No headache, doctor. Sleep is sound. I read a few pages and I am off.
[SEG0014] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In the evening he asks me, three four times, whether the gas is switched off. Same question, same tone, as if it is the first time.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I am only being careful about the gas, doctor. That is prudence in an old house, not an illness.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): I hear you. I should say plainly, I am not going to announce any diagnosis today. I need the old background first. What long-standing problems are there?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Only blood pressure, for many years. Otherwise, by God's grace, I have kept well.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure, ongoing, yes, that is what the old card says too. Any operation, any hospital admission?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation, doctor. I have never been admitted.
[SEG0020] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The tablets, since he will not remember the names. Morning he takes amlodipine, and Ecosprin after food. At night, atorvastatin.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): Doses I need, not just names. Sister, what does the last prescription in the file actually say?
[SEG0022] person_1 (NURSE): The file says amlodipine 5 mg once daily, atorvastatin 20 mg at night, and aspirin 75 mg in the morning.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Amlodipine is not 5, sister. Last month the colony physician changed it to 10 mg. The file was not updated, the new strip is at home.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I would not like to mislead you, doctor. I do not know the milligrams. I swallow what she places in my hand.

[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, so I am looking at 5 mg in the file and 10 mg in the house, and I will not pretend I know which one is true. The atorvastatin 20 at night and the aspirin 75 in the morning, are those at least agreed?
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes, those two are correct. Only the amlodipine I am changing, I mean, it is already 10. He does not skip, I watch him take them.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): She is very particular, and I am regular. I have no complaint about the tablets.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. Casting my mind back, any old blood report, sugar or cholesterol, that you were told about?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Last year, at the health camp near our colony, they checked my sugar. They said it was borderline. They did not tell me a figure, only that word, and I never started a sugar tablet.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Borderline, no number. I will keep that only as what they told you, not as a value I can chart. And no diabetes tablet, that is clear.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): There is more, doctor. He misplaces the spectacles and then says I have hidden them. At the bank he forgot why we were standing in the queue.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): The spectacles were on the fridge, where you yourself had kept them. And the bank was for the passbook update. I had told you that in the auto.

[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Several small episodes, each with a different telling. I am not going to stitch them into a disease name in this room. Any fall, any weakness of the hand or the speech, any chest pain?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): None of that, doctor. No fall, no weakness, no chest pain. I still walk to the park on most mornings.
[SEG0035] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The walking is true. But last Tuesday, after the market, he was out almost two hours. Normally he is back in forty minutes.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Two hours is, if I may say, an exaggeration. I stopped to speak with Mr. Deshpande about his grandson's admission. It was not more than an hour, and I knew the road.

[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Park most mornings, I will put that down as a good thing. I am thinking we should not lean on that old borderline sugar. I would like fresh bloods: full count, sugar fasting and after food, kidney function, thyroid, and B12.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): If you consider it necessary, doctor, I will certainly cooperate. I do not wish to be obstinate.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And his memory, will someone test it properly? I cannot keep being the only one who notices.

[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. I will arrange a memory assessment. Let me explain what that is: a structured look at memory and thinking, done with our counsellor. It is not a verdict, and I am not naming any illness today.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand, and I am grateful for the explanation. I still feel, if I may say, that this is my wife's worry more than any disease in me.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Both of those views can be true enough to write down. Sister, please book fasting bloods for this week, and the memory assessment in the next open slot.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): Fasting bloods I can give Thursday, 8.30 in the morning, collection room. The memory slot I still have to confirm, I will phone.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thursday we can do. Should he still take the morning tablets if he is fasting?
[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, the morning tablets with a sip of water only, no tea and no food. And until we see a bit more clearly, please do not send him to the market alone.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I have managed that market for thirty years, doctor. Still, I will follow what you advise. I do not want to add to her distress.
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thank you. I want you both back once the reports and the memory assessment are in. Let us say in about two weeks, a little either side if the slot slips.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two weeks is fine. I will keep every paper in one plastic folder, otherwise it vanishes.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): We will attend, doctor. You have taken the trouble to explain, and that I appreciate.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): Today's 152 over 88 is a little higher than I would like, but a single reading, with this dose muddle, is not enough for me to change any tablet.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Please don't change it today, I am already holding two different strips in my head.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): I will not. What I do need is both amlodipine strips, the 5 mg and the 10 mg, brought next time so the number is settled by looking, not by memory.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): She will bring them. About the strips, I admit, I may not remember which packet is which.
[SEG0054] person_1 (NURSE): So, Thursday 8.30, fasting, collection room. Memory assessment time is not fixed yet, I will telephone the house once the counsellor replies.
[SEG0055] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Phone me, sister, not him. If you tell him, the message may not reach me.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): I do pass messages, generally. But yes, phone her. That is the practical course.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sister will phone the wife. If Thursday is missed we still want the bloods within the week, though let us plan on Thursday itself.
[SEG0058] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We will not miss it. I have already told the neighbour not to expect him for the morning walk that day.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, you have been most courteous. I remain of the opinion that I am well, and yet I will come for both the tests, as you wish.
[SEG0060] person_4 (DOCTOR): That is all I am asking. We will sit again in about two weeks with whatever has come back, and only then talk about meaning. No name for this today.
[SEG0061] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thank you, doctor. Come, the auto stand is just outside. I have the card in my bag.
